designIntentSource.title: The different lightspeed methods
designIntentSource.role: Governing design intent for family-specific emergency de-transit, predictive safety, differentiated machinery, and mathematically credible transit engineering.

purpose: Define dependency-graph and shared-resource scheduling rules for FTL abort operations so emergency duration is derived from explicit precedence, bounded operation times, resource capacities and declared arbitration rather than guessed sum/max behavior.
invariants: Operation duration, precedence and resource demand are independent evidence classes.
Precedence-only schedules use the longest directed path through the operation DAG.
Two operations may overlap only when precedence permits overlap and every modeled renewable resource remains within certified capacity.
When concurrent demand exceeds capacity, an explicit authority must provide serialization/arbitration or the schedule is UNRESOLVED; the runtime does not invent priority.
A shared-resource conflict is not repaired by averaging demand over the full abort interval.
Consumable energy and instantaneous renewable power are separate constraints.
Unknown task duration, missing required dependency, missing required capacity, cyclic dependency, or invalid resource demand is never converted to zero.
A derived schedule may increase the current intervention upper bound; it may not reduce the certified baseline without explicit recertification authority.
PRECOMMIT and PORTAL_ADMISSION families retain their own route semantics; this authority schedules machinery operations only.
Race-specific hardware may realize abstract resources differently without changing dependency mathematics.

mathematics.precedenceEarliestStart: ES_i = max(EF_j) for all j in predecessors(i), with ES_i = 0 for source operations
mathematics.criticalPath: Any source-to-sink directed path whose summed bounded durations equals T_DAG
mathematics.renewableCapacity: For every modeled renewable resource r and all t: sum_{i active at t} q_{i,r} <= C_r
mathematics.consumableReserve: For consumable resource e: sum_i E_{i,e} <= E_available,e unless an explicit replenishment model is supplied
mathematics.energyFromPower: E_i = integral(P_i(t) dt); constant bounded power approximation E_i <= P_i,upper * d_i,upper only when that approximation is explicitly valid
mathematics.scheduledIntervention: T_int,current >= max(T_stage,current, T_schedule) unless explicit recertification authorizes a smaller baseline

commandNetwork.notes: Routing continuity alone does not prove latency or simultaneous command capacity.

solverCompute.notes: Use only when a compute-capacity authority exists.

protectedPower.notes: Instantaneous deliverable electrical/mechanical equivalent power; separate from stored energy.

energySinkPower.notes: Certified rate at which stored field/transition energy can be accepted or dissipated.

coolingRejection.notes: Heat rejection or transport capacity during the modeled short transient.

actuatorAuthority.notes: May represent thrust-vector, field-former, vane, aperture, coupling or other bounded actuator capacity.

hydraulicFlow.notes: Especially relevant to Mur'rek vane/control machinery when established by source authority.

referenceBus.notes: Q-lattice, manifold, fold, phase and gate reference/synchronization networks.

protectedEnergy.notes: Stored emergency reserve. Do not use as an instantaneous power certificate.

generatorRequirements: Emit a stable operation id, bounded duration or duration source, predecessor ids, resource demand and provenance for every scheduled operation.
Emit every modeled resource capacity with unit, lower certified capacity bound and provenance.
Do not infer an operation order from object enumeration, narrative order, species, technology tier or file order.
When a resource conflict requires serialization, emit the authoritative serialization edges or named arbitration policy that created them.
Preserve unscheduled/UNRESOLVED status when multiple legal orderings exist and no authority selects one.
Carry the schedule makespan and limiting/critical operations into dynamic escape evidence.
Preserve source terminology and family identity separately from scheduling mechanics.

failureCodes.AOS-CYCLE: Dependency graph contains a directed cycle.
failureCodes.AOS-DURATION-UNKNOWN: A required operation lacks a bounded duration.
failureCodes.AOS-DEPENDENCY-MISSING: An operation references a predecessor not present in the packet.
failureCodes.AOS-CAPACITY-MISSING: A required renewable resource lacks certified capacity.
failureCodes.AOS-CAPACITY-EXCEEDED: A single operation exceeds certified resource capacity.
failureCodes.AOS-CONTENTION-UNRESOLVED: Otherwise concurrent operations exceed capacity and no authority provides arbitration/serialization.
failureCodes.AOS-ORDER-CONFLICT: Declared serialization contradicts existing precedence or creates a cycle.
failureCodes.AOS-PROVENANCE-GAP: Required scheduling evidence lacks source provenance.
